payload.title: Using Surrogate Series with Pyleoclim
payload.summary: This Jupyter notebook provides an overview of the SurrogateSeries class in the Pyleoclim library, focusing on generating and visualizing surrogate data to assess the significance of various analyses. It covers both parametric and non-parametric surrogate generation methods, including autoregressive models and phase scrambling. The notebook demonstrates how to fit surrogates to specific datasets like the Southern Oscillation Index and LR04, and discusses their use in significance testing. The notebook concludes with a discussion on the application of surrogates in non-parametric tests.
goals: Learn how to generate and visualize surrogates with Pyleoclim
Learn how to use surrogates to assess the significance of various analyses

section_blurbs.blurb: The notebook begins with an introduction to the Pyleoclim library and its capabilities for generating surrogate series.
section_blurbs.heading: Notebook start

section_blurbs.blurb: This section introduces the SurrogateSeries class and the general concept of surrogates, explaining their importance in significance testing.
section_blurbs.heading: Using Surrogate Series with Pyleoclim

section_blurbs.blurb: Explains the generation of parametric surrogates using Gaussian white noise and autoregressive models, demonstrating how to sample from models and visualize results.
section_blurbs.heading: Parametric Surrogates

section_blurbs.blurb: Demonstrates how to fit surrogate models to specific datasets like the Southern Oscillation Index, using spectral analysis to determine appropriate null models.
section_blurbs.heading: Fitting surrogates to a target: the Southern Oscillation Index

section_blurbs.blurb: Discusses the application of surrogate series in evaluating the significance of statistical analyses, comparing different surrogate methods.
section_blurbs.heading: Uses for significance testing

section_blurbs.blurb: Introduces non-parametric surrogate generation methods, highlighting their advantages when no clear parametric model is available.
section_blurbs.heading: Non-parametric surrogates

section_blurbs.blurb: Covers the generation of surrogates that match the temporal pattern of unevenly spaced observations, using AR(1) models as an example.
section_blurbs.heading: Unevenly-spaced surrogates

section_blurbs.blurb: Summarizes the key points about the use of surrogates in non-parametric tests and the capabilities of the Pyleoclim library in generating and analyzing surrogate data.
section_blurbs.heading: Takeways
